# A finite joint critical-menu and supporting-facet allocation alternative

This is an exact finite first-order interface, not a Gamma inequality.
It keeps circuit selection before the resulting obstruction, permits
inside allocations to be prescribed, and retains the outside allocation
in the response. The finite assumption is explicit: the chosen body
velocities are constant on each actual fiber facet. General potentials
which vary along a coincident facet are not discretized without proof.

## 1. Actual geometric setting and finite data

Let d>=1 and let P be a finite lattice-complete base. Let K_z be positive
full-dimensional common-normal simplex fibers of an actual convex body.
Write M=sum_z |K_z|. Their finitely many facets are indexed by l; each
index specifies its integer base, outward continuous unit normal, and
actual facet F_l. Put A_l=H_(d-1)(F_l)>0. Counting measure is used if d=1.

Choose a finite-dimensional polyhedral cone V of actual compatible
one-sided body variations. For v in V their outward normal velocities
are constants r_l(v) on the facets F_l, linear in v. Then

    m(v)=M'(0+)=sum_l A_l r_l(v).                              (1)

One genuine class is supplied by the normal-bundle support-roof erosion
construction: use finitely many signed normal-dependent affine physical
functions and nonnegative convex-potential directions, whose restrictions
to each actual facet are constant. The cone imposes nonnegative
coefficients on the latter; signed coefficients are unrestricted. The
actual bodies are defined by

    u dot x + epsilon V_v(u,z,x) <= h_z(u),

with z in the original projection. Convexity of V_v in physical variables
and concavity of the actual roof h_z give actual compatible bodies. The
archived uniform interior/radius and radial-derivative proof gives (1).
This includes base hinges, uniformly localized facets, and radial facet
weights on a simplex. It does not include an arbitrary nonconstant
facet tent in this finite theorem.

Fix actual deepest sources Y_i and a finite menu of closed nonvertical
critical caps through each source. Every cap has raw mass Q=beta M.
Normalize its continuous normal to unit length, and write H_j={ell_j>=0}.
For each menu list finitely many positive circuits c, with fixed positive
coefficients rho_cj satisfying

    sum_(j in c) rho_cj u_j=0.                                (2)

They may be the extreme positive circuits of the finite normal menu;
then there are finitely many and each uses at most d+1 caps. For each
choice, its original affine weighted margin is assumed nonnegative on
the assigned deepest base planes. The fixed-witness theorem supplies
this hypothesis for its circuits. Threshold shifts s_j with

    sum_(j in c) rho_cj s_j<=0                                (3)

therefore preserve the whole-plane CLOSED cover exactly: the weighted
sum of the new margins ell_j-epsilon s_j remains nonnegative. Copies of
one cap in different groups may be shifted separately.

For global depth conclusions, retain finite uniformly slack covers at all
unassigned bases, including their persistence for the actual variation.
The conclusions below about strict depth descent include this premise.
The finite alternative itself concerns the displayed critical groups.

Each cap must have positive proper coarea S_j>0. In particular this holds
when its source is interior to its own positive fiber. S_j is the sum of
H_(d-1) of its proper sections, since the continuous normal is normalized.
Supporting facets are classified separately as I_j (body inside the cap)
and O_j (body outside, zero captured d-volume). Strict full/empty fibers
and zero-area supporting sections require no extra allocation.

Let a_jl be the H_(d-1) measure of the portion of F_l strictly inside H_j.
Coincident facets are omitted from a_jl. Define B_j(v)=sum_l a_jl r_l(v).
All these are actual geometric measures, not free scalar data.

## 2. Exact finite piecewise-linear cap derivative

For threshold motion H_j(epsilon)={ell_j>=epsilon s_j}, the raw derivative
is

    D_j(v,s_j)=B_j(v)-S_j s_j
        +sum_(l in I_j) A_l min(r_l(v),-s_j)
        +sum_(l in O_j) A_l max(r_l(v)-s_j,0).                 (4)

Here S_j includes only proper sections. At an inside supporting facet the
outward coordinate t satisfies body t<=epsilon r_l and cap t<=-epsilon s_j;
its signed thickness is their minimum. At an outside facet the body is
t<=epsilon r_l and cap t>=epsilon s_j, giving the positive-part thickness.
These signs also hold for d=1 endpoints. Proper sections give ordinary
coarea. The remaining boundary neighborhoods contribute o(epsilon) by
bounded displacement and continuity from above of surface measure away
from the finitely many coincident facets. Thus (4) includes positive
supporting boundary mass; no closed indicator is substituted for an
allocated trace.

Because r_l is constant on its facet, (4) has FINITELY MANY linear
branches. For fixed v it is continuous, strictly decreasing in s_j with
slope at most -S_j<0, and ranges from +infinity to -infinity.

## 3. Exact quantile response and the nonconvex selection objective

For each row let s_j(v,q) be the unique inverse of D_j(v,s_j)=q. For a
circuit c, the strictly decreasing continuous function

    q -> sum_(j in c) rho_cj s_j(v,q)

has opposite infinite limits. Thus there is a unique q_c(v) satisfying

    D_j(v,s_j)=q_c(v) for all j in c,
    sum_j rho_cj s_j=0.                                      (5)

It is continuous, positively homogeneous, and piecewise linear in v.
For the last assertion, choose for each minimum/maximum in (4) one of its
two branches and impose its linear branch inequalities. On that region,
(5) is a finite linear system; its threshold coefficients are strictly
negative and the final weighted scalar coefficient cannot vanish. The
finitely many resulting polyhedral regions cover all v, including their
seams. Their formulas agree at shared points by uniqueness.

For fixed v and c, the following are equivalent:

    q_c(v)<beta m(v);                                         (6)

    there exist shifts satisfying (3) with
    D_j(v,s_j)<beta m(v) for every j in c.                     (7)

Indeed (6) gives the equalized shifts (5). Conversely (7) and strict
monotonicity imply s_j>s_j(v,beta m(v)); taking weighted sums shows the
inverse sum at beta m(v) is strictly negative, hence beta m(v)>q_c(v).

Therefore favorable menu selection has the exact finite objective

    exists v in V such that
    max_i min_(c in menu_i) [q_c(v)-beta m(v)] < 0.            (8)

This expression is generally neither convex nor concave. No minimax
exchange or selection-independent response vector is claimed. Each
chosen circuit and its threshold shifts give an actual first-order
upper bound on its entire assigned base planes. With the slack-cover
premise, (8) implies a strict decrease of global normalized maximum depth
for sufficiently small positive epsilon. Finiteness makes all o(epsilon)
remainders harmless AFTER a strict direction is found.

## 4. A finite family of LPs with the exact allocation order

For each chosen cap copy, choose a binary inside branch alpha_jl in{0,1}:

    min(r_l,-s_j)=min_(alpha in{0,1})
                      [alpha r_l-(1-alpha)s_j].

For outside facets introduce binary kappa_jl in{0,1}, with
max(r_l-s_j,0)=max_kappa kappa(r_l-s_j). Define the linear form

    D_j^(alpha,kappa)(v,s_j)=B_j(v)-S_j s_j
       +sum_(I_j) A_l[alpha_jl r_l(v)-(1-alpha_jl)s_j]
       +sum_(O_j) A_l kappa_jl[r_l(v)-s_j].                   (9)

Then (8) is EQUIVALENT to

    exists one circuit c_i for each group,
    exists binary inside choices alpha,
    exists v in V and shifts obeying all (3),
    for EVERY binary outside choice kappa on each chosen cap,
       D_j^(alpha,kappa)(v,s_j)-beta m(v)<0.                  (10)

Proof: for a given actual direction choose the minimizing inside branch
on every coincident facet; then maximizing outside branches gives exactly
(4). Conversely, (4) is at most the maximum of (9) for ANY chosen inside
branches, so (10) gives strict actual descent. The order of the two
existential choices and v may be interchanged; the outside universal
quantifier may not be moved ahead of them.

For a fixed circuit tuple and fixed alpha, put all (9) for all outside
vertices into one linear feasibility system, together with v in V and
(3). Replace strict negative bounds by <=-1: this is equivalent by
positive homogeneity and finitely many rows. Thus (10) is decided by a
FINITE UNION of LP feasibility problems. This is a finite nonconvex
alternative, not one silently convexified LP. Continuous inside values
are unnecessary for exact existence; they remain legitimate sufficient
upper branches, but binary choices already attain each true minimum.

## 5. The opposing stress and its dependent response weights

Fix a circuit tuple and an inside choice alpha. Let D be the polyhedral
cone of (v,s) specified by v in V and (3), and let

    f_jkappa=D_j^(alpha,kappa)-beta m.

Exactly one of the following holds:

* There is (v,s) in D with all f_jkappa(v,s)<0.
* There are lambda_jkappa>=0, sum lambda_jkappa=1, such that

      sum lambda_jkappa f_jkappa(v,s)>=0 for all (v,s) in D.   (11)

This is the finite Gordan/Farkas alternative, obtained by separating the
polyhedral image of D from the open strictly negative orthant. The two
statements cannot both hold by substitution. The separating functional
has nonnegative coefficients and is nonzero, so its sum can be normalized
to one.

Aggregate lambda_j=sum_kappa lambda_jkappa. On a cap with lambda_j>0,
the average outside allocations

    sigma_jl=sum_kappa lambda_jkappa kappa_jl/lambda_j

belong to[0,1]. Correlations among outside branches do not matter because
(9) is additive. Conversely every such vector sigma is a convex mixture
of its binary vertices. The effective section coefficient is

    T_j=S_j+sum_(I_j) A_l(1-alpha_jl)
                 +sum_(O_j) A_l sigma_jl >0.                 (12)

Testing (11) on the shifts alone proves that for each circuit group i
there is k_i>=0 such that

    lambda_j T_j=k_i rho_cj for all j in c_i.                 (13)

Indeed the shift coefficient is -lambda_j T_j. A linear functional is
nonnegative on {s:rho dot s<=0} exactly when it is -k rho with k>=0.
Inactive groups have k_i=0 and all their lambda_j=0. In an active group,
write Lambda_i=sum_(j in c_i)lambda_j and

    theta_j=(rho_cj/T_j)/(sum_(h in c_i)rho_ch/T_h).

Then lambda_j=Lambda_i theta_j and sum_i Lambda_i=1. The allocated body
trace of cap j equals its strict indicator off coincidences, alpha_jl on
inside facets, and sigma_jl on outside facets. The resulting group profile
is its theta-weighted sum.

For the pure potential cone r=-Phi, (11) becomes precisely

    sum_i Lambda_i integral Phi W_i^(alpha,sigma) d eta
                   <= beta integral Phi d eta               (14)

for every chosen nonnegative potential combination; signed directions
impose their additional moment equalities. Thus the stress can choose
both its group weights and its outside allocations, and those allocations
also change theta through T_j. Treating theta as independent of sigma
would give the wrong game.

Consequently NO finite-class descent means:

    for EVERY selected circuit tuple and EVERY binary inside choice,
    there EXISTS an opposing stress (Lambda,sigma) satisfying (11)--(14).

The stress may change with the circuit tuple or inside choice. This is
the finite exact counterpart of the archived universal-inside-allocation
stress theorem. It does not yield one common stress for all choices.

## 6. The regular overlap matrix and genuine joint improvement

When there are no supporting facets, T_j=S_j and each circuit profile
W_ic is fixed. Normalize finitely many admissible potentials Phi_h by
integral Phi_h d eta=1 and restrict to Phi=sum_h a_h Phi_h, a>=0,sum a=1.
Set

    A_(ic),h=integral Phi_h W_ic d eta.

The exact best joint payment in this finite class is

    max_(a in simplex) min_i max_(c in menu_i) sum_h A_(ic),h a_h
      = max_(c_1,...,c_s) max_(a in simplex)
                            min_i sum_h A_(i,c_i),h a_h.      (15)

This equality merely combines finitely many EXISTENTIAL choices: for
fixed a each group independently chooses its best circuit. For each
fixed circuit tuple the inner maximum is one LP. It is not an exchange
with adversarial stress weights or allocations.

The individual-efficiency summation rule retains only diagonal entries
of a chosen test matrix. Equation (15) retains every off-diagonal entry:
one test may pay several witnesses, and one witness may use a different
circuit for that same test. Therefore joint payment can be strictly
stronger even when no supplied test pays Gamma at an individual witness.
For an algebraic illustration, two identical rows (c,c), c>0, have joint
value c; splitting two individually normalized c-tests by the harmonic
rule only guarantees c/2. This is an illustration of the comparison rule,
not a claim that arbitrary such matrices are actual critical geometry.

For nonsmooth caps, the counterpart is (8) or (10), not (15) with an
independently chosen allocation profile. In particular taking the worst
outside allocation separately AFTER optimizing each individual witness
can lose the fact that one actual body variation controls all groups;
taking convenient outside allocations before the variation is unsound.

## 7. Mandatory exact calibrations and scope

The R4 product has one deepest base and an actual prescribed diagonal
circuit with efficiency40/93<4/9 for the ENTIRE convex-potential cone.
That is a lower bound on neither (15) nor the selected-menu value. The
same product has a symmetry orbit of an actual critical cap whose common
base tilt exposes a fiber on which every selected cap is full; its
localized radial/base potential pays1. A menu containing that orbit must
show this good choice. A menu containing only the diagonal circuit need
not. R4's depth40/93 is above its OC target1/9, and this example is not an
attained bad minimum.

Here are the two exact calibration dependencies and the required transfer.
The all-normal depth and uniqueness input for R4 is proved in
`candidate de93c4f08837e128`;
the prescribed-profile cone bound is in
`candidate b78a2eb10bd3783f`.
For clarity, uniqueness follows directly once the depth lower bound is
known. A deepest point cannot lie strictly inside any canonical cap:
raise its threshold slightly while retaining that point, thereby removing
positive volume from its proper zero-slice sections and producing mass
less than Q. Thus every canonical margin at a deepest point is <=0;
their sum is zero, so every margin is zero. Hence
lambda_j=1/3-ell_j(z). Since ell_j(z) is an integer and 0<=lambda_j<=1,
all ell_j vanish. This forces z=0 and lambda_j=1/3 for every j.

The sharp binary-times-simplex product gives the opposite calibration.
Put N=2^n, let p range over {0,1}^n, and take the canonical centroid cap
circuit on the p-fiber, tilted to strictly miss every other fiber. Denote
its profile by W_p. These are genuine critical circuits: own-fiber
Grunbaum gives raw depth Gamma_d |K|, and the circuits cover every fiber
at exactly that mass. The full facet convex-order theorem in
`candidate 8e69e6820cd6ee00`
proves, on EACH simplex facet and for every nonnegative convex restriction,

    integral_(boundary K_p) Phi W_p d eta
                   <= Gamma_d integral_(boundary K_p) Phi d eta.

Its proof includes d=1, where each boundary endpoint has profile1/2.
A normal-dependent potential restricts to an ordinary convex function on
each fixed-normal facet, so the inequality applies separately and sums.
W_p vanishes on other fibers. Consequently

    min_p integral Phi W_p d eta / integral Phi d eta
       <= (1/N) sum_p integral Phi W_p d eta / integral Phi d eta
       <= Gamma_d/N.

Equality is attainable. For each base p its nonnegative Hamming-distance
hinge (1-L_p(z))_+ is one on p and zero on every other binary base. The
facet theorem has equality for constants on each facet; all fibers have
the same surface area. The sum of these hinges is one on every measured
base and gives each group ratio Gamma_d/N. Thus the exact common optimum
for these fixed isolating profiles is Gamma_d/2^n. This proof does not
claim that arbitrary profile choices have the same upper bound; it is
the required sharp fixed-profile calibration. Equation (15) cannot create
cross-fiber credit for these profiles by summing the same mass twice.

The unequal nonlattice three-site example blocks every attempt to infer
the sharp arithmetic constant from (4), (11), and first-order criticality
alone. Lattice completeness and the original occupied-parity budget must
enter a later quantitative estimate. The present finite alternative
requires no Gamma estimate and proves none. It also does not imply that
an unrestricted extremizer admits a sufficient finite constant-on-facet
potential class, or that every critical menu has a regular subcircuit.
Those are separate geometric questions, now with a precise finite test.

## 8. An actual nonsmooth calibration with arbitrary inside choices

Take the complete three-fiber product {-1,0,1} times [-1,1], d=1,
with Y=(0,0). Its mass is6 and actual maximum raw depth is3: symmetry
gives at least half the mass at Y, while complementary continuous caps
give the upper bound at every point. Consider the two genuine critical
caps H_+={x-z>=0} and H_-={-x+z>=0}, with rho_+=rho_-=1.
Each has one proper own section, one inside endpoint coincidence, and
one outside endpoint coincidence. Thus neither may be treated by the
regular closed-indicator formula.

Let r_L(z),r_R(z) be any compatible first-order endpoint velocities,
measured outward. Write

    L=r_L(-1), R=r_R(1),
    B_+=r_R(-1)+r_R(0), B_-=r_L(0)+r_L(1),
    m=B_++B_-+L+R.

For cover-equality shifts s_+=s, s_-=-s, formula(4) gives

    D_+=B_+-s+min(L,-s)+max(R-s,0),
    D_-=B_-+s+min(R,s)+max(L+s,0).

The elementary min/max identities yield D_++D_-=m for EVERY s.
Strict monotonicity therefore makes the common equalized derivative
q=m/2. This agrees with the exact fact that the shifted caps are
complements up to zero mixed-volume boundary and have total mass M_epsilon.
No deformation can produce a strict first-order improvement from this
fixed complementary cap menu, irrespective of compatibility details.

Prescribe arbitrary inside allocations A on the left endpoint of fiber-1
for H_+, and B on the right endpoint of fiber1 for H_-. They need not be
binary for this check. Choose the opposite outside allocations to be
1-A and1-B respectively. Then both effective section coefficients equal

    T_+=T_-=1+(1-A)+(1-B)=3-A-B>0.

The cap weights lambda_+=lambda_-=1/2 satisfy(13), and their allocated
body traces sum to one on every endpoint. Thus their weighted profile
is exactly1/2 everywhere, proving(14) with beta1/2 for EVERY prescribed
inside pair(A,B). This is a concrete actual calibration of the dependent
outside allocation, not a free scalar allocation menu or a new d=1
centerpoint theorem.
